body: Tentatively slated for 5.4 M1 for _team discussion_.
I added `@TestMethodOrder(Alphanumeric.class)` to the example and verified that `test2()` always fails on `master`.

Inserting `Thread.interrupted();` as the first line in `org.junit.platform.engine.support.hierarchical.NodeTestTask.execute()` allows the example test class to execute correctly.

@junit-team/junit-lambda, As for whether or not that is the correct location to invoke `Thread.interrupted();` is open for discussion.
I have removed the `Vintage` label since the invocation of JUnit 4 tests is handled by the corresponding JUnit 4 `Runner` which is not under the control of the `VintageTestEngine`.
**Team Decision:** Reset the flag before/after executing a `Node`.

issue.body:
## Overview

Whenever a test case sets the thread context `ClassLoader`, the test runner thread keeps using that `ClassLoader` for the following tests. This causes failures when combined with Mockito and mocks of package private classes/interfaces.

## Expected Behavior

When the thread is reused to run another test, the context `ClassLoader` should be reset to the original one.

## Steps to Reproduce

To reproduce the problem I created this example repo: https://github.com/bacer-esteco/junit5-bug-report.

Just run the 'test' task.

This problem is reproducible using both Jupiter and Vintage (tried on version 5.4.0), launching the test both from Gradle 5.2.1 and IntelliJ IDEA 2018.3 (and previous).

## Related Issues

- #201
- #1688

issue.title: Interrupted state of main thread not cleared after test causes unrelated tests to fail

repository.name: spock
repository.description: The Enterprise-ready testing and specification framework.

issue.body:
# Issue description
If a tests sets the java.lang.Thread.currentThread().interrupted() flag, this flag is not cleared  after the test (on the main thread). This can cause issues in other tests, namely spring boot tests for example that are really hard to track down. It would be great if spock would call:

Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted(true);  // on main thread

to avoid this issue. 

JUnit solved this here: https://github.com/junit-team/junit4/issues/1365

# How to reproduce

class InterruptIssueSpec extends Specification {

    def "setting state"() {
        Thread.currentThread().interrupt()
        expect:
        true
    }

    def "checking state"() {
        Thread.sleep(4000)
        expect:
        Thread.currentThread().isInterrupted() == false
    }

}


## Java/JDK
11

## Groovy version
spock-core:1.3-groovy-2.5
